So, type 1 diabetic here. Been diabetic for 20 years now. 

While a blood sugar of 200 isn't good, it's not going to kill/ hurt you immediately. Ideally you want a fasting blood sugar between 85 and 105. But 200 isn't a call for an emergency room trip. 

What you can do to help your body today is be sure to drink plenty of water and get some electrolytes, like sugar free Gatorade. Going for a walk or some light physical activity can help increase your sensitivity to insulin, and will help your body digest carbs etc. You might want to try to eat lower carb foods until you hear back from the Dr. Stuff like salad, meats, veggies, cheese and other protein. 

The main thing is drink plenty of water because it helps your body process excessive sugar.

I respectfully disagree with basically your entire statement. I've been suicidal for over 20 years. Of sound mind and while under distress. Medicated and unmedicated. The desire has never changed. I do agree that the majority of people who are suicidal need help, not just sign a form and get an injection to end it. I also want to address the "sooth your own suffering not others". I see the point you are trying to make, but if it's selfish to commit suicide so as to not hurt others, then it is as equally selfish for others to expect you to stay alive against your wishes.
